transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-28 15:00 UTC · duration ~49m · attendees listed above

Summary: Quick sanity check and operational runthrough of Redwood's BYO-HSM integration and proposed crypto-ops on-call playbook. Veridian is evaluating a private deployment path with customer-managed HSM for key custody, needs clarity on guardrails: emergency rotation, key escrow, audit trail, SSO/RBAC controls, and network egress.

Topics: BYO-HSM connector, TLS in-transit guarantees, envelope encryption, KMS key lifecycle, HSM failover, escrow, SOC 2 audit evidence, RBAC and SSO mapping, playbook for on-call rotations and emergency key compromise response.

Action items (discussed verbally; see action_items list above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Hannah Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got like 50 minutes, so we'll try to walk through the playbook and then leave time for questions. I'm Hannah from Redwood, AE. Diego and Lena are our SEs.
[00:12] Dr. Priya Rao: great, thanks, Hannah. quick context: Veridian is moving sensitive assay metadata into a model-backed service. Compliance wants customer-controlled keys — they asked for BYO-HSM evaluation.
[00:22] Hannah Kim: understood. the goal today is to show how Redwood supports BYOK via HSM connectors, what the failover story looks like, and how the on-call crypto ops playbook would operate.
[00:30] Diego Martinez: quick callout — there are two common modes we see: full key custody via your HSM (we call it external KMS), or Redwood-managed keys with bring-your-own-wrapping keys. both have tradeoffs.
[00:44] Samir Patel: when you say external KMS, what's the exact connection pattern? do we do an mTLS tunnel to an HSM appliance in our DC or a cloud-HSM endpoint?
[00:54] Diego Martinez: both supported. our connector can perform mutual TLS to cloud-HSM APIs (e.g., AWS CloudHSM, Azure KeyVault HSM endpoints) or to an on-prem gateway that proxies to an HSM appliance. typical flow: model inference service requests envelope key from Redwood runtime, runtime issues KMIP/PCKS or cloud API call to your HSM, gets wrapped DEK back.
[01:12] Elena Gomez: mm-hmm. and we want to avoid any plaintext key material leaving our vault. so the question is: does Redwood ever see keys in the clear in any path?
[01:20] Diego Martinez: no. design is envelope encryption: the DEK (data encryption key) is generated in the runtime but immediately wrapped by your KMS/HSM and Redwood stores only wrapped keys. if you choose full external key generation, your HSM can generate the DEK and return a wrapped DEK — Redwood never has the unwrapped key. caveat: some legacy connectors require a short-lived session key, but we have mitigations.
[01:36] Dr. Priya Rao: about audit logs — our auditors expect immutable evidence of key usage: who requested the key, timestamp, operation type. can Redwood forward or correlate HSM usage logs with request traces?
[01:48] Lena Park: yes, we can correlate. runtime emits request-level trace IDs and stores token-level audit entries in our audit log. for BYOK, we ingest the HSM operation events (push/pull) via a secure webhook or aggregated syslog depending on your environment and then correlate on trace id. note: the HSM's native logs remain authoritative for crypto ops.
[02:05] Thomas Reed: network question — we run an egress proxy and private endpoints only. what's the required egress pattern for cloud HSMs? we can't open everything.
[02:13] Diego Martinez: we'll provide a minimal IP/FQDN allowlist and mTLS fingerprint. for on-prem gateway, we just talk to an internal address, so no internet egress is required. we'll need a small set of ports for health checks and for the runtime <-> gateway comms.
[02:25] Elena Gomez: emergency key rotation: say a key is suspected compromised at 0100 on a Sunday — what's the playbook? does Redwood support immediate revocation and rewrap of all DEKs?
[02:34] Marcus O'Neil: short answer: yes, but caveats. Redwood supports instant revocation flags and a forced fallback model — traffic can be routed to a fallback key or a lower-tier model that uses a different key while we perform rewrap. we provide tools to bulk rewrap DEKs using a new master key. must coordinate with your HSM for policy.
[02:52] Dr. Priya Rao: we need a documented runbook for on-call rotation steps: who contacts which HSM administrator, how the orchestration runs (automated vs manual), verification checks, and rollback.
[03:02] Hannah Kim: that's exactly what the playbook draft covers — we'll share the link. it includes escalation paths, CLI commands and API calls, recommended smoke tests (sample inference request patterns), and an auditor-friendly checklist.
[03:15] Samir Patel: about key escrow — auditors sometimes expect a dual-control escrow to recover keys if the HSM is destroyed. do you support storing an encrypted escrow copy in a separate region or with a third-party escrow provider?
[03:26] Diego Martinez: yes, options include: (1) customer-managed escrow within their HSM cluster; (2) encrypted backup to customer-controlled object storage with envelope encryption using a secondary HSM key; or (3) third-party escrow partners. each option has different SLA implications.
[03:37] Elena Gomez: is there a way to test failover without touching production keys? we want a rehearsal flow.
[03:43] Lena Park: absolutely — POC harness can provision a test key and run a dry-run rotation against a staging dataset. Diego will set that up in the POC.
[03:50] Dr. Priya Rao: SSO/RBAC mapping: we require granular role separation — crypto ops cannot see application tokens, and engineers cannot perform key deletion. how do you model RBAC for KMS actions?
[04:01] Diego Martinez: Redwood's control plane provides role-based policies. you can map your SAML groups to roles (e.g., crypto-ops-admin, key-operator, auditor). we support just-in-time admin elevation for emergency ops and audit trails for any elevation. we also integrate with SCIM for group sync.
[04:15] Samir Patel: our internal policy also mandates hardware attestation for any HSM nodes. we use TPM-backed attestation. can you validate attestation attestations? (laughs)
[04:26] Hannah Kim: yes — for private deployments we can verify attestation proofs and include attestation reports in the onboarding checklist. note: cloud-HSM services vary. we documented supported attestation flows in the playbook.
[04:36] Elena Gomez: one subtlety — tokenization path for PII: we want deterministic tokens for lookup but random for downstream model calls. is that supported with your envelope model?
[04:47] Diego Martinez: you can configure the DEK usage so that deterministic derivation uses a KDF with per-tenant salt inside your HSM. Redwood can orchestrate the KDF call under the HSM policy so plaintext never leaves. for downstream model calls we use ephemeral DEKs.
[04:58] Thomas Reed: audit retention and export — auditors want signed exportable logs for 7 years. what can Redwood provide?
[05:06] Lena Park: we support long-term export to customer-controlled S3 with object-level signing (optional), and we can stream logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders. retention policies are configurable.
[05:16] Dr. Priya Rao: SOC 2 evidence — can you provide an itemized mapping of Redwood's controls vs our SOC2 policy statements? we need to show logging, separation of duties, incident response.
[05:26] Marcus O'Neil: yes, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II report and a controls mapping template. we also attach audit trails for any BYOK flows used during the POC.
[05:35] Hannah Kim: quick demo segment? Diego, do you want to screen-share the playbook and a sample key rotation? (note: screen-share referred to but not recorded in transcript).
[05:44] Diego Martinez: i'll narrate — step 1 generate test key in HSM; step 2 provision key binding in Redwood; step 3 run smoke inference; step 4 flip key alias; step 5 bulk rewrap job. i should call out timing — bulk rewrap depends on dataset size and batch window; for large token volumes we recommend a staged roll.
[06:05] Elena Gomez: are there throttles or rate limits from Redwood during rewrap? we can't have tokenization blocked for hours.
[06:12] Diego Martinez: rewrap is a background job; we throttle to respect latency SLOs. you can opt for a priority rewrap which runs faster but may impact per-request latency briefly. we'll surface cost and latency impact in the console.
[06:24] Samir Patel: any regulatory issues with cross-border key backup? we have EU data residency constraints.
[06:29] Lena Park: escrow backups can be region-locked to EU regions; we support multiple geographic vaults. if keys must never leave the EU, you can keep HSMs and backup storage in-region and configure runtime to only use EU endpoints.
[06:40] Dr. Priya Rao: encryption-in-transit question: we need to prove TLS 1.3 with mutual auth end-to-end from client to HSM gateway — can Redwood attest to that in logs?
[06:50] Diego Martinez: yes, we record TLS version and mTLS fingerprint in connection metadata, and that can be included in the correlated audit record.
[06:58] Elena Gomez: what about key rotation frequency — auditors like scheduled rotation plus emergency rotations. can Redwood automate scheduled rotation policies?
[07:07] Marcus O'Neil: scheduled rotation policies are supported — specify frequency, rotation window, and rollout policy (immediate vs staged). rotation itself is orchestrated with your HSM according to your policy.
[07:18] Thomas Reed: curious about HSM firmware upgrades — can we enforce maintenance windows?
[07:22] Hannah Kim: yes, maintenance windows and planned outage scheduling is supported for private deployments; we also provide a maintenance mode to drain traffic and failover.
[07:31] Samir Patel: are there known limitations with particular HSM vendors? we use a mix — one on-prem Thales, one cloud vendor in EU.
[07:39] Diego Martinez: we have tested flows for major vendors (Thales, Utimaco, AWS CloudHSM, Azure KeyVault HSM). edge cases exist for older KMIP versions; we'll document required firmware/API minimums in the onboarding checklist.
[07:52] Elena Gomez: for the POC, can we do a tabletop of an incident and simulate an on-call response?
[07:58] Lena Park: yes, we'll include a tabletop script in the playbook and run a dry tabletop during the POC week.
[08:05] Dr. Priya Rao: last thing — we need assurance about crypto key escrow access controls. if an escrow backup is stored in S3, who can unseal it? we want dual control and M-of-N unseal flows.
[08:16] Diego Martinez: supported pattern: backup wrapped with a recovery key that is split using Shamir (m-of-n) and stored with separate custodians. Redwood can integrate that pattern into the backup automation; the unseal requires multiple custodians to provide their shares.
[08:29] Samir Patel: good. that's about it for high-level questions.
[08:33] Hannah Kim: great. quick recap of next steps — we'll share SOC2 report, the HSM/BYOK runbook, and set up the POC calendar. Diego will own the POC prep. Elena will own on-call verification and Samir provides the network diagram.
[08:47] Dr. Priya Rao: thanks all. we'll review the docs and come back with any additional control-specific asks.
[08:53] Hannah Kim: thanks, everyone. wrapping up now.

Notes about transcript quality: there are a few mis-heard words and occasional speaker attribution mistakes (e.g., Marcus and Diego overlapping at 02:52). The document refers to a playbook link and internal deck: https://redwood.example.com/docs/byo-hsm-playbook (placeholder link).

End of transcript.
